summary: Full end-to-end verification of Notion-style sharing (Phase 1) — backend authorization + share endpoints + frontend Dashboard/ShareDialog/CanvasPage integration. 16/16 pytest cases pass in /app/tests/test_sharing.py (owner-only share GET/PUT, member CRUD, invite validation, 'shared with me' listing without owner-field leakage, viewer/editor/owner scene RBAC, anonymous access via ?share= viewer link, denial when link_access='none', bad token rejected, rotate-link invalidates old, workspace-domain sharing for non-public domain example.com + teammate visibility). 12/12 UI flows pass via Playwright: owner sees dashboard + ProjectCard menu (Rename/Delete) + MCP-ready badge, share dialog opens, invite-by-email works, link-access → Viewer exposes share-link-input + copy + rotate (token changes), workspace-access-select present, user B sees Shared-with-me section with role-badge and NO owner menu / NO share button on the canvas, anonymous with valid viewer token loads canvas read-only with 'View only' role-badge and hidden share button, anonymous with link_access=none is redirected to landing page. Regression test_gateway.py still 15/16 — one legacy assertion (test_isolation_user_b_cannot_see) now sees 403 instead of 404 on GET /api/projects/{id} because that endpoint switched from _owned_project (404) to require_access (403) as required by the sharing model. This is intentional API surface change tied to sharing; PATCH/DELETE still return 404 for non-owners (owner-only).
action_items: OPTIONAL: Update legacy /app/tests/test_gateway.py::test_isolation_user_b_cannot_see to accept 403 on GET /api/projects/{id} (the endpoint intentionally moved from owner-only 404 to access-check 403 to support sharing). Not a bug — semantic tightening.

OPTIONAL polish: RoleBadge on CanvasPage renders 'View only'/'Comment only' but the Dashboard shared-card variant renders 'Editor'/'Viewer'. Both use data-testid='role-badge'; consistent copy would be nicer but not blocking.

OPTIONAL: server.py resolve_access grants link-based role even when link_access is 'commenter' or 'editor' for signed-in users — good. For anonymous users it correctly caps to 'viewer'. Consider explicitly documenting this in the endpoint description.
critical_code_review_comments: resolve_access() correctly composes highest role across (owner | member | workspace | link) with anonymous link capped to viewer — good design.
_project_view() correctly hides owner-only fields (agent_token, share_token, workspace_domain) from shared users. Verified via test_shared_with_me_appears_for_invitee.

list_projects() includes members-by-email and workspace-domain projects — verified end-to-end. Sorting by (is_owner, updated_at) desc means shared canvases always sink below owned, matching the Dashboard split.
share_token rotation: rotate-link generates a new token and old token immediately fails (401 for anon). Solid.
PUT /projects/{id}/share validates workspace_domain presence before enabling workspace_access — good defensive check.
Minor: DELETE /projects/{id}/members reads email from query string only. The frontend passes it via axios params → OK, but documenting this (or accepting body too) would be more RESTful.

Minor: ShareDialog RoleSelect for members offers 'commenter' but the RoleBadge on Dashboard hardcodes only Editor/Viewer labels — a member with role=commenter would show a blank/undefined-looking label. Since KISS scope is viewer/editor, either remove Commenter from ROLE_OPTS or extend RoleBadge to cover it.

success_rate.backend: 100% (16/16 sharing + 15/16 legacy regression, 1 intentional semantic change)
